Search Gram feasibility for targets below the record by alternating projections between capped-diagonal and rank-23 PSD sets with Burer-Monteiro row-normalized extraction and penalty-homotopy tangential refinement plus short LP polish.
direction: Attack the problem through the Gram matrix with an SDP-style feasibility search rather than point-space basin hopping. For target values \(t\) below the record, such as \(0.04755,0.04745,0.0473,0.0470\), seek a \(54\times54\) matrix \(G\) with unit diagonal, \(G_{ij}\le t\), positive semidefiniteness, and rank at most 23 using alternating projections or Burer–Monteiro factorization \(G=YY^{T}\) with \(Y\in\mathbb R^{54\times23}\): project onto the diagonal/entrywise-cap constraints, project onto rank-23 PSD matrices by eigendecomposition, and use Dykstra correction or a penalty homotopy. Extract points from the leading 23 eigenvectors whenever the residual is small, then apply tangential smooth optimization and a short LP polish; also record the smallest infeasibility residual as evidence for which \(t\) and which pair pattern merit point-space refinement.

idea: Enforce a 6x9 block ansatz from non-contact spectral/clique clustering then anneal a smooth inter/intra-margin objective with reassignment before LP polish.
direction: Extract and enforce the suspected block structure, then release it gradually. From `best.npy`, build non-contact graphs at several slack thresholds such as \(10^{-3},3\times10^{-3},10^{-2}\), cluster their complements using spectral clustering or greedy clique cover, and test partitions near \(6\times9\) without assuming them in advance. Starting from the resulting assignment, optimize the points with a smooth objective that penalizes violations of \(\langle x_i,x_j\rangle\le t\) for inter-block pairs, penalizes \(\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-(t-\delta)\) above zero for intra-block pairs with a margin \(\delta\) initially around \(0.002\)–\(0.01\), and lightly penalizes unequal inter-block cosines to preserve the block ansatz; periodically reassign points according to their current non-contact neighborhoods. Anneal the intra-block margin and equality penalties to zero, retain the best feasible configuration encountered, and finish with at most 20 seconds of trust-region LP under a hard 165-second total deadline.

idea: Discrete Golay/Hadamard/sparse candidate pool with greedy best-hole construction plus exhaustive one-for-one and top-K two-for-two swaps, then annealed repulsion and trust-region LP polish.
direction: Search a discrete algebraic candidate pool completely different from the record. Generate candidates from cyclic binary Golay \((23,12,7)\) codewords mapped to \(\{\pm1\}^{23}/\sqrt{23}\), sign/permutation variants of sparse patterns with supports of sizes 4–8, vectors obtained by deleting one coordinate from Hadamard-24 rows, coordinate vectors \(\pm e_i\), and normalized \(\pm e_i\pm e_j\) patterns; deduplicate perhaps \(50{,}000\)–\(200{,}000\) candidates. Precompute candidate-to-selected inner products incrementally, build a 54-set by repeated best-hole insertion followed by exhaustive one-for-one and occasional two-for-two swaps minimizing first the maximum and then the number of pairs above thresholds near the record, and only then continuously polish the selected set. This can reveal Golay/Hadamard-type topology that perturbations of the incumbent cannot reach.

idea: Memetic search over contact-graph basins with Procrustes-aligned greedy recombination and rigid-block rotations / block hole-reinsertion, pre-screened by cheap softmax repulsion and finished by trust-region LP.
direction: Run a diversity-preserving memetic search using whole-cluster rigid motions and Procrustes recombination, with strict time accounting. Maintain a small population of locally polished configurations distinguished by their thresholded contact graphs or inferred block partitions; align parents by orthogonal Procrustes, form children from their 108-point union by greedy max-cosine selection, and mutate children by rotating one inferred block as a rigid body through a random two-dimensional plane by \(0.05\)–\(0.5\) radians, by jointly rotating two blocks oppositely, or by deleting and greedily reinserting an entire block into the largest spherical holes. Pre-screen children with a few hundred cheap softmax/Adam steps, LP-polish only the best one or two, keep a child only if it improves the incumbent or has a materially different contact graph at comparable score, checkpoint the incumbent throughout, and stop all exploration by 150 seconds so the final LP and return occur before 170 seconds.

Search cyclic C23 orbit ansatz with three seeds and greedy best-8 selection using annealed LogSumExp Riemannian Adam then gradual symmetry breaking and one final LP polish.
direction: Search a symmetry-restricted orbit ansatz before releasing symmetry: use the cyclic group $C_{23}$ acting by coordinate shifts in $\mathbb{R}^{23}$, generate two full orbits of 23 points from two seed vectors, and generate the remaining 8 points as the best 8 shifts of a third seed; this reduces the initial search to three seed vectors plus selection of the partial orbit. Optimize the seeds with Riemannian Adam on a LogSumExp approximation to the maximum inner product, annealing the inverse temperature from about 50 to 800 over 2000 steps and trying at least 30 random seed triples under a strict 120-second timer. Then break the symmetry gradually by adding tangent noise of sizes $10^{-3},3\times10^{-3},10^{-2}$, run cheap smooth optimization after each release, retain the best few distinct candidates, and reserve only the final 20 seconds for one trust-region LP polish.

idea: Escape the jammed optimum along collective soft rigidity modes with LogSumExp Adam screening and contact-graph clustering plus rare LP snaps.
direction: Escape along collective rigidity modes rather than independent Gaussian kicks: build the tangent-space rigidity matrix for pairs within $10^{-6}$ of the current maximum, compute its lowest eigenvectors and an approximate equilibrium stress, and displace all points along random combinations of the five softest modes with amplitudes between 0.03 and 0.30, since these coordinated motions can change contact topology without immediately creating a very large inner product. After each modal kick, run only 300–600 steps of vectorized LogSumExp Adam, screen by the true maximum cosine, and cluster accepted candidates by their thresholded contact graph so that repeated returns to the incumbent basin are discarded. Impose a hard internal deadline of 160 seconds, check time inside every optimization loop, permit at most a handful of 2-second LP calls for candidates below a preset screening threshold, and reserve 15 seconds for the final polish.

direction: Perform targeted delete-and-rebuild surgery on the frozen record instead of perturbing all 54 points: repeatedly choose a subset of 5–8 points forming a dense contact clique, the lowest-contact points such as those visible near indices 17, 23, 26, and 27, or a random subset biased toward high-contact points; freeze the remaining points and jointly re-optimize only the removed points. For the subproblem, generate at least 200,000 random sphere candidates plus candidates obtained by Riemannian Adam minimizing a smoothed maximum against both frozen and other rebuilt points, allowing the subset several seconds at most and abandoning it if its smoothed score is not competitive. Cycle through many subsets with a contact-graph hash archive to avoid rebuilding the same topology, use no full LP during the cycles, and LP-polish only a candidate whose cheap smooth score is within about $0.002$ of the incumbent or already below it.

idea: De novo tight-frame continuation with diverse Gaussian, low-discrepancy, Hadamard and sparse-sign starts optimized by batched Riemannian Adam on centroid plus tight-frame plus p-norm of positive overlaps with fading weights and rising p, then one LP trust-region polish of the distinct basin.
direction: Run a genuinely de novo tight-frame search that ignores the record until the final comparison: initialize 16–32 configurations in parallel from random Gaussian points, spherical low-discrepancy points, rescaled $\{\pm1\}^{23}$ Hadamard-type patterns with one coordinate pattern removed or projected, and sparse sign vectors, then optimize a continuation objective beginning with frame/centroid penalties $\|\sum_i x_i\|^2$ and $\|X^\top X-(54/23)I\|_F^2$ plus a $p$-norm of positive pairwise inner products for $p=8,16,32$, and gradually fading the frame penalties while increasing $p$ to 128–512 to approach the true minimax objective. Use batched Riemannian Adam or L-BFGS for at most 110 seconds, maintain a diversity archive based on sorted pairwise-cosine profiles so that one basin cannot dominate, compare the best new basin directly with the record, and spend the remaining time on a single LP polish of the best structurally distinct candidate rather than polishing every restart.

idea: Block-rotation orbit construction with antipodal order-46 group plus truncated second orbit, optimized over seeds then symmetry-broken
direction: Symmetry-constrained fresh construction, then symmetry breaking: Abandon the record basin entirely and search over orbit configurations under a fixed finite orthogonal group, e.g. let Q be a block-diagonal rotation acting as rotation by 2π/23-like angles on eleven 2D coordinate planes plus a sign flip on the last coordinate (order 46), and parameterise the code as full Q-orbits of 1–2 free seed vectors plus a short orbit/polar points to total exactly 54 points, optimising only the seeds with tangential Adam on a LogSumExp max objective (k 50→1000, 3000 steps, several random seeds). Take the best symmetric result, break symmetry by adding tangent noise of size 0.01–0.05 to all points, re-optimise unconstrained with Adam, and finish with a single LP polish (exploration ≤ 140 s, polish ≤ 30 s, internal cutoff 170 s). An orbit-structured start enforces the organised, non-hairball contact topology the incumbent lacks and may land in a genuinely different basin rather than a perturbation of the record.

idea: Null-projected random soft modes from the jammed contact rigidity matrix give feasible collective escapes screened by fast LogSumExp Adam and rare short LP polish.
direction: Rigidity-nullspace collective escape: From best.npy, build the contact set with slack < 1e-6, construct per-point tangent bases (54×22 via SVD of each x_i's null space), assemble the rigidity matrix A (contacts × 1188 tangent coordinates) whose rows are the linearised contact gradients, and compute its 25–40 smallest right singular vectors (use scipy.sparse.linalg.svds on A, or eigendecomposition of the 330×330 Gram AAᵀ for speed). Generate trial configurations by displacing along random sign combinations of 2–5 of these softest modes with total tangent step sizes in {0.03, 0.08, 0.15, 0.25}, retract to the sphere, screen each trial with a fast LogSumExp tangential Adam phase (300–600 steps, k annealed 100→600, lr 0.005, numpy only, no LP), and LP-polish only trials whose smoothed max is within 0.004 of the incumbent; cap total exploration at 140 s, reserve 25 s for one final LP polish, and hard-stop all loops by an internal 170 s deadline. This targets motion the jammed optimum can actually accommodate instead of wasting trials on contact-violating random kicks.

idea: Jointly delete a connected high-contact cluster (or low-contact set) and greedily reinsert k points from 30k random candidates then refine movables with tangential Adam LogSumExp plus short full Adam and trust-region LP polish.
direction: Joint delete-and-reinsert of a jammed cluster (multi-point topology surgery): Identify a connected high-contact cluster by thresholding the Gram matrix at the max minus 1e-4, taking a seed max-pair and its shared neighbours, and deleting k ∈ {6, 8, 10, 12} points at once (cycling over several clusters/seeds and also over the lowest-contact points in indices ~17–35 suggested by the middle panel). With the remaining 54−k points frozen, reinsert the deleted points jointly: sample 30,000 random unit candidates, greedily pick k candidates minimising the running maximum inner product against frozen plus already-chosen points, then optimise only the k movable points with tangential Adam on a LogSumExp objective (1500 steps, k_exp 80→800, lr 0.01) while frozen points stay fixed, unfreeze everything for a short Adam phase, and only then run a 5–8 s trust-region LP polish; accept strictly on true max cosine, keep the global best, and iterate until a 150 s exploration cutoff before a final 20 s LP polish. Jointly relocating a whole cluster can change contact topology in a way the repeatedly-failed single-point reinsertions cannot.

idea: Escape the over-jammed 330-contact optimum with collective multi-point void reinsertion plus masked two-stage annealing that freezes the background while the hole subset settles, then releases globally, using only LP-free moves until a short final squeeze.

Basin-hopping from the record with void-reinsertion and collective subset kicks followed by fast annealed soft-max tangential repulsion and a final trust-region LP snap for heterogeneity-driven escape.
Incremental continuation from 40 to 54 points with best-hole insertion and LP-free LogSumExp Adam re-annealing, multiple seeds then single LP polish.
direction: Continuation in N with hole insertion and LP-free annealing: Build codes incrementally from scratch — start from a well-optimised random 40-point code (LogSumExp Adam, k annealed 30→500 over 2000 steps), then insert points one at a time up to 54, each time placing the new point at the best of 50,000 random candidates (minimising max inner product to the current set) followed by a global Adam re-anneal of all points (800 steps, k 100→700, lr decaying 0.01→0.002) so the whole configuration reorganises around each addition instead of freezing early contacts; run 3–4 independent continuation chains with different RNG seeds inside a 145 s budget, scoring chains by true max cosine and discarding any chain more than 0.01 behind the incumbent after reaching 54 points. Only the single best final configuration receives a trust-region LP polish in the remaining ~25 s. Growing the code through a sequence of less-jammed smaller problems is a principled route to a contact graph with natural slack heterogeneity and possibly a few near-rattlers, which perturbations of the fully-jammed 54-point record have failed to produce.

idea: Project random tangent kicks onto the nullspace of the contact rigidity matrix to move along collective soft modes that preserve contacts to first order, then screen with fast LogSumExp tangential Adam and LP-polish only promising trials.
direction: Rigidity-nullspace collective escape: From best.npy, build the contact set with slack < 1e-6, construct per-point tangent bases (54×22 via SVD of each x_i's null space), assemble the rigidity matrix A (contacts × 1188 tangent coordinates) whose rows are the linearised contact gradients, and compute its 25–40 smallest right singular vectors (use scipy.sparse.linalg.svds on A, or eigendecomposition of the 330×330 Gram AAᵀ for speed). Generate trial configurations by displacing along random sign combinations of 2–5 of these softest modes with total tangent step sizes in {0.03, 0.08, 0.15, 0.25}, retract to the sphere, screen each trial with a fast LogSumExp tangential Adam phase (300–600 steps, k annealed 100→600, lr 0.005, numpy only, no LP), and LP-polish only trials whose smoothed max is within 0.004 of the incumbent; cap total exploration at 140 s, reserve 25 s for one final LP polish, and hard-stop all loops by an internal 170 s deadline. This targets motion the jammed optimum can actually accommodate instead of wasting trials on contact-violating random kicks.

idea: Fast LP-free basin hopping with void reinsertion and cap-cluster collective moves screened by annealed soft-max tangential heavy-ball descent to find a sparser-contact basin.
Delete a whole jammed contact cluster and jointly reinsert it via greedy void filling plus frozen-subset LogSumExp Adam before LP polish.
